title: Deterministic Retry & Stream Framing SDK Requirements (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Avery Chen
description: PRD: Define cross-language SDK requirements for predictable retry behavior and a compact, versioned stream-framing protocol. The goal is to ensure Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs behave identically for common edge cases: transient failures, duplicate requests, partial stream resumes, and mixed-mode clients (sync + streaming). Deliverables: language bindings spec, deterministic backoff policy, idempotency contract, streaming frame schema, reference harness and interop test matrix.
background: Customers embed Redwood inference into latency-sensitive paths and depend on consistent SDK semantics. Current divergence across language SDKs causes subtle bugs: different backoff jitter, inconsistent idempotency token handling, and varying behaviors on stream reconnects. Those issues surface as duplicate completions, message reordering in streaming, and unpredictable tail-latency. This ticket consolidates requirements and acceptance criteria for a coordinated SDK rollout.
scope: In scope: spec for retry/backoff semantics, idempotency tokens and header propagation, streaming frame format (chunk metadata, offsets, finalization markers), resume semantics (server snapshot cursor format), language-agnostic test vectors, and compatibility shims for older SDK versions. In-scope SDKs: Python, TypeScript, Go. Out-of-scope: deep runtime kernel changes, server-side batching strategies, and UI/console changes beyond release flags.
out_of_scope: Model serving kernel optimizations, Dedicated capacity autoscaler changes, or modifying existing backend APIs that would break current clients without an opt-in feature flag.
requirements: Deterministic retry policy: SDKs must implement the same base algorithm: initial delay 100ms, exponential factor 2.0, max delay 8s, capped total retries 5, and configurable full-jitter window. The default MUST match these values across languages unless explicitly overridden by the app.

Idempotency contract: All mutating calls (where server can de-duplicate) must accept an optional idempotency_token. SDKs should generate RFC4122 v4 tokens by default when not provided and expose a way for callers to opt-out. Token propagation must be logged in client telemetry.
Request identification: Each outgoing logical request must carry a stable 'x-rw-request-id' header. On retries the header value must remain constant so server-side correlation is possible.

Structured stream frames: Define a compact JSONL frame envelope: {"type","seq","cursor","meta","payload"} (versioned). Frames must include monotonically increasing seq numbers to allow reordering detection and deduplication by clients.

Resume semantics: Server offers 'cursor snapshots' at well-defined commit points. SDK resume API must accept a server cursor string and replay only missing frames. Resume must be idempotent: re-applying an already-processed seq should be a no-op.

Message ordering: Streaming clients must present a best-effort in-order view to callers. Out-of-order frames from the wire must be buffered up to a configurable window (default 50 frames) and reassembled by seq number.

Partial chunk handling: Large responses can be chunked; SDKs must expose a streaming iterator that yields complete logical messages (assembled from chunks) to the application — no application-level chunk assembly required.
Backward compatibility: Introduce a 'stream_version' negotiation header; SDKs must fall back to legacy framing when connecting to older servers and expose a runtime warning when features are bumped.

Configuration surface: SDKs must expose the same set of options (backoff policy struct, max_retries, idempotency token generator hook, resume buffer_size, stream_version override) and document language-specific defaults.
Reference implementations: Provide a canonical implementation of the retry algorithm and frame parser in a small, language-agnostic pseudocode repo and short code snippets for Python/TS/Go.
Telemetry: SDKs must emit events for retry attempts, final failure, resume happened (with cursor), and duplicate-frame-detected (seq). These events must include the stable request id.
Feature gating & rollout: New behavior must be behind an opt-in SDK flag 'enable_deterministic_retries_and_framing' for at least one release to allow guided migration.
Docs & migration guide: Provide migration steps, common pitfalls, and a compatibility matrix describing behavior when mixing old and new SDKs and server versions.
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement the deterministic retry algorithm and pass the reference interop test vectors for: transient 5xx, connection reset, and idempotent duplication scenarios.

Streaming frame format implemented and compatible: a client connects to a server with stream_version=2 and receives chunked messages that reassemble into logical messages in-order for 99.999% of test runs across emulated packet reorder conditions.

Resume test: A streaming session that is interrupted at seq N can be resumed using the server cursor; client receives frames for seq > N without duplicates or gaps in the provided logical message stream.
Idempotency test: Replayed client requests with identical idempotency_token do not create duplicate side-effects in the test harness for mutating endpoints.
Interop test matrix completed and green: combinations include new SDKs vs old SDKs, new server vs old server, and mixed-language clients connecting to the same session where applicable.
SDKs emit the required telemetry events with stable x-rw-request-id and events surface in the debug logs for at least the first rollout customers.
Migration docs, API reference, and code snippets published in the SDK repos and internal docs; release notes prepared for the public changelog.
Backward compatibility warning: When an SDK connects to a server with older stream_version, it logs a single warning explaining limitations and suggesting upgrade paths.
technical_notes: Prefer full-jitter backoff (sleep = random(0, base * 2^attempt)) to reduce thundering herd issues; provide knobs for switching to equal-jitter if needed.
Sequence numbers must be 64-bit unsigned to avoid wraparound for long-lived streams; cursor snapshots should include the last-committed seq and a short opaque token for server validation.
Frame envelope must be intentionally minimal to reduce per-token overhead for small messages; binary payload allowed as base64 for transport where necessary.
Reference pseudocode to be placed in the sdk-interop repo: retry_backoff.py, retry_backoff.ts, retry_backoff.go and frame_parser.{py,ts,go}.
Consider using an internal feature flag endpoint to coordinate staged rollout: SDKs query a 'compatability_flags' endpoint on startup when enabled.
Add unit tests that simulate packet reorder, duplicate delivery, and delayed duplicate frames; use local harness to strictly assert in-order delivery to user callback.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Ship SDK changes behind opt-in flag. Provide CLI and env var to enable flag. Target small set of internal customers and 2 external beta customers.
Phase 2 (interop tests): Run the full interop test matrix between SDK branches and server staging. Fix any language-specific divergence.
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): Flip flag default to ON for new minor runtime SDK versions, but keep server-side compatibility for older SDKs for at least two server releases.
Phase 4 (deprecation): After 6 months and no major regressions, announce deprecation of legacy framing with migration guides and a scheduled removal window.
Rollback: Each SDK release includes a runtime switch to immediately disable the deterministic behavior if critical regressions appear.
test_plan: Automated unit and integration tests for the retry policy across languages with deterministic RNG seeds to validate jitter windows.
Chaos tests: Simulate TCP connection resets, packet reorder, and duplicate frames at scale in CI. Verify no message corruption and bounded buffering behavior.
Interop CI job: Matrix job that runs pairwise language combos (py-ts, py-go, ts-go) against server versions (v1 legacy, v2 framing).
Performance regression checks: measure throughput and p99 tail latency for streaming with default buffer size and ensure <5% regression compared to legacy framing.
Telemetry validation: ensure events are emitted and correlated by x-rw-request-id in test logs.
